title: Skyline: Stacked workspace lanes and progressive-collapse navigation prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Proposal and prototype for a stacked 'lane' approach to the Console sidebar that surfaces multiple workspace layers (global workspace, project lanes, run-time routes) with progressive collapse to preserve density while keeping discoverability. Includes a cost-lens peek for rapid token/cost troubleshooting and quick-route keyboard navigation.
goals: Reduce switch friction when users work across 3+ workspaces or routes
Expose per-lane cost and latency signals without forcing a full dashboard hop
Make rollouts and route-level controls discoverable and one-click accessible
Provide a responsive design that preserves SLO visibility at small widths
constraints: Console left rail has fixed vertical real estate on 1280px width; must support both compact and expanded states
Must not change existing API endpoints or break route IDs used by Engineering (no backend work required for initial prototype)
Telemetry events must remain GDPR-friendly; avoid adding new PII-level identifiers
Keyboard navigation must remain consistent with current command-palette bindings
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows stacked lanes with three levels: Workspace -> Project lane -> Route (or dashboard)
Clicking a lane focuses Console content and highlights active lane; keyboard arrows navigate lanes
Cost-lens hover displays last 24h token cost and 95th percentile latency for that lane
Usability test (n=8, mix of platform and product engineers) achieves median task time < 45s for switching between non-adjacent lanes
Design sign-off from PM (Marco Ruiz) and Eng lead (Sofia Alvarez) recorded in PRD and review notes
design_notes: Stack metaphor: lanes are arranged visually to imply hierarchy; use depth shadow and subtle separators instead of heavy borders
Progressive collapse behavior: on narrow widths lanes collapse to icons + compact cost badge; on hover expand to full label and cost-lens
Cost-lens is a lightweight widget (sparkline + token count + latency badge) — clicking it brings up the full cost analytics page
Consider accessibility: ensure ARIA labels for lane groups and ensure focus order follows visual stacking
We iterated 3 variants in Figma: 'overlay flyout', 'inline stack', 'split-pane'; the current recommendation is 'inline stack' for lower context switching cost
